what.text: Ibutamoren (code names MK-677 and MK-0677) is a small, non-peptide molecule taken by mouth. It mimics ghrelin and acts on the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, making the pituitary release more growth hormone and raising IGF-1. It was studied by Merck from the 1990s.

what.text: Ibutamoren is not an approved medicine. FDA has placed it in Category 2 for compounding because of a heart failure safety signal. Using it for sleep is off-label and outside any approval.

research.text: Ibutamoren has been tested in several randomized trials in older adults, people after hip fracture and people with Alzheimer’s disease. Only one small study, from 1997, measured sleep. A hip fracture trial was stopped early because of heart failure. Trials in children with growth hormone deficiency are ongoing.

research.title: Sleep in young and older adults, 1997

facts.v: young group: double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-period crossover (5 mg, 25 mg, placebo at bedtime); older group: two treatment periods (2 mg, then 25 mg) compared with baseline
8 young adults aged 18 to 30; 6 older adults aged 65 to 71
7 days per period (young); 14 days per period (older)
sleep stages by polysomnography; hormones

research.found: In young adults, the 25 mg dose increased stage 4 (deep) sleep by about 50% and REM sleep by more than 20% vs. placebo. In older adults, REM sleep rose by nearly 50% and REM latency fell. We found no larger sleep trial.

src.label: Copinschi et al., Neuroendocrinology, 1997

research.title: Two years in healthy older adults, 2008

facts.v: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, modified crossover
65 healthy adults aged 60 to 81
2 years (main results at 1 year)
GH and IGF-1, lean mass, belly fat, strength, function, glucose, cortisol, bone

research.found: GH and IGF-1 rose to young-adult levels. Lean mass rose 1.1 kg vs. a 0.5 kg fall on placebo, but strength and function did not change. Weight rose 2.7 kg vs. 0.8 kg. Fasting glucose rose and insulin sensitivity fell. Cortisol rose. Sleep was not a measure.

src.label: Nass et al., Ann Intern Med, 2008

research.title: Recovery after hip fracture, first trial, 2004

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 13 centers in Europe, Canada and the US
161 previously mobile hip-fracture patients aged 65 and over
6 months, then 6 months follow-up
physical function tests, Sickness Impact Profile, independent living, IGF-1

research.found: IGF-1 rose 84% vs. 17% on placebo. There were no significant differences in function or overall health scores.

src.label: Bach et al., J Am Geriatr Soc, 2004

research.title: Recovery after hip fracture, second trial (stopped early)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IIb, multicenter
123 older hip-fracture patients (62 on ibutamoren 25 mg a day, 61 on placebo)
planned 24 weeks
physical function, IGF-1, falls

research.found: IGF-1 rose by 51 ng/mL. Gait speed improved, but stair climbing and most other function measures did not. The trial was stopped early because of a safety signal of congestive heart failure in a limited number of patients. The authors concluded the drug has an unfavorable safety profile in this group.

src.label: Adunsky et al., Arch Gerontol Geriatr, 2011

research.title: Alzheimer’s disease progression, 2008

facts.v: double-blind, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled
563 people with mild to moderate Alzheimer’s disease; 416 completed
12 months
standard scales of cognition, daily function and dementia severity

research.found: IGF-1 rose 73% at 12 months, but there was no difference from placebo on any scale.

us.text: Ibutamoren is not FDA approved for any use. FDA has placed it in Category 2 for both 503A and 503B compounding, meaning it raises significant safety risks. Products sold labelled “for research use only” are not legal to sell for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: a search of FDA’s drug approvals data for ibutamoren found no matches. It is being tested as LUM-201 in a phase III trial in children.

items.text: ibutamoren mesylate was added to Category 2 for 503B on December 29, 2022 and for 503A on September 29, 2023. FDA states: “Ibutamoren mesylate poses significant safety risks due to the potential for congestive heart failure in certain patients. The agency is aware of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial assessing ibutamoren mesylate for the treatment of patients recovering from hip fracture that ‘was terminated early due to a potential safety signal of congestive heart failure.’”

after.text: Ibutamoren is prohibited at all times under WADA class S2.2.4, growth hormone releasing factors, which names “growth hormone secretagogues (GHS) and their mimetics [e.g. anamorelin, capromorelin, ibutamoren (MK-677), ipamorelin, …].” All S2 substances are non-Specified. unconfirmed: The 1997 sleep study abstract does not say how the older group’s results were compared (it describes baseline data and two dose periods, without placebo).
We could not confirm whether the 2008 older-adult trial recorded sleep; the abstract does not mention it.
Status in the UK, the EU and Australia was not checked against a regulator record (TGA’s ARTG search did not load; EMA search was blocked).

A Merck hip fracture trial registered as NCT00128115 (protocol 0677-032, terminated, 83 enrolled) may be the trial Adunsky et al. reported with 123 patients; the numbers differ and the link was not confirmed.
Published results of the LUM-201 trials in children were not reviewed.
surprises: The only sleep study of ibutamoren had 14 people and FDA has put it on its Category 2 safety list after a hip fracture trial was stopped for heart failure.
It is not abandoned as a drug: as LUM-201 it entered a phase III trial in children with growth hormone deficiency in May 2026.
